source.prompt: A Canada jay (gray jay, Perisoreus canadensis) of the Pacific Northwest, one adult bird perched with its wings folded tight against the body, side-on pose. NOT a blue jay, no crest. Realistic proportions, about 29 cm long with a long tail; a fluffy rounded body, a round head, a short stubby black bill. Soft grey back, wings and tail, a white forehead, throat and collar, a dark grey cap on the back of the head, a pale grey-white belly. Dark legs, three toes forward and one back. No base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: Scaled to 0.29 m bill to tail. The preview's long fanned tail (rising to the top of the head; seen from the front it was the 'tuft' behind the crown) and the drooping primaries cut off at the rump and replaced by a long, narrow, rounded tail (13 cm, 2.2-4.2 cm wide, 8 degrees below level, faint pale tip); no crest (the preview's crown is smooth once the tail is gone); body levelled 4 degrees; generated legs replaced by black procedural legs; small dark eye; flight wing cards (rounded, faint pale tips on lod0). Colours (the Pacific 'Oregon' form, P. c. obscurus): white forehead, face, throat and collar; dark grey-brown cap from the crown down the nape, with a dark spot behind the eye; brownish-grey back, wings and tail, faint pale fringes on the folded wing (lod0); pale grey flanks and whitish-grey underparts; black bill and legs. Triangles: lod0 1,000 = 811 body + 189 legs, tail, cards and eyes; lod1 400 = 309 + 91; lod2 120 = 91 + 29. GLB 172,560 bytes.

rig: bird rig template of the Steller's jay (tools/build_stellersjay.py; drawn with client/src/animalModels.js RIG.stjay's constants): PART BODY 0, LEG_A 1 / LEG_B 2 procedural legs (pivot at the knee), TAIL 3 procedural tail (pivot at the rump), HEAD 6 (head and neck, pivot at the base of the neck), WING_L/R 4/5 and HAND_L/R 9/10 flight cards that collapse into the shoulder on pose; extras.rig {kind 'bird', wing (shoulder), tail (rump), head (neck base), length_m}; no skin
accuracy_notes: Built 2026-11-05. Reads as a fluffy grey jay with a white face and a dark cap and nape, a short black bill and a long narrow tail; clearly not the Steller's jay. Still open: the cap's lower edge is jagged on lod1/lod2 (large faces); the white collar shows on the neck sides and throat but blends grey at the back; the legs are a little long; the eye is a small black dot (no pale eye-ring, correct for the species). A local birder should check the extent of the dark nape against Olympic birds.
